subject: Mutual Action Plan + perf eval: hardware comparison for pilot
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@datapilot.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com, soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan + perf eval: hardware comparison for pilot

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion I put together a short mutual action plan and a proposed evaluation matrix we can run during the 2-week pilot. Goal: establish a repeatable performance profile (TTFT, p95 latency, sustained throughput, concurrency envelope) across three candidate hardware footprints so you can pick cost vs latency tradeoffs for production.

Quick asks from DataPilot to lock the plan:
- Confirm model checkpoint (we expect the 13B causal model variant you mentioned).
- Confirm region (you said us-west-2 is preferred).
- Provide ~200 sample prompts (anonymized) and a 5-10k token prompt set if available.

Proposed KPIs (examples — happy to tighten):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) median and p95 target: prefer TTFT < 60ms median, p95 < 200ms for interactive flows.
- End-to-end p95 latency for 512-token streams.
- Token throughput @ steady-state concurrency (tokens/sec and tokens/sec/GPU).
- Max sustainable concurrent streams with p95 < 300ms.

Evaluation matrix (test each cell):
- Full GPU: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40S-48GB
- MIG/partitions: A100 (1/2/4-way), H100 (1/2/4-way) using same model shard layout
- Workloads: single-stream TTFT, steady-state 50/100/200 concurrent streams, 512-token and 2x512-token long-run tests

Deliverables from Redwood:
- CSV with per-run metrics (TTFT distribution, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec), run logs, and command lines.
- Short recommendation (cost vs latency tradeoff) and sizing guidance for 3 production profiles (pilot, growth 1, growth 2).

Attached: MAP-Datapilot-v2.pdf (timeline, responsibilities), runbook-harness.sh (test harness). I can schedule the runs as soon as you confirm the model + dataset.

If that looks good I propose we target start week of May 22 for runs and a 2-week evaluation window.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: MAP-Datapilot-v2.pdf (PDF 180KB), runbook-harness.sh (script stub)
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@datapilot.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan + perf eval: hardware comparison for pilot

Thanks Ava — this looks like a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Model: we will provide the 13B-medium checkpoint (float16) and a fixed tokenizer. Please ensure the harness uses our tokenization script (I attached a small wrapper to this reply).
2) Region: confirmed us-west-2.
3) KPI tweak: our product team prefers p95 <= 180ms for interactive features. Can we aim for that?
4) Cost sensitivity: procurement will ask for an estimated $/1M tokens range for each hardware footprint (including MIG). Please include GPU hourly + inferred per-token calculation.

We can provide a 300-sample prompt set and a 6k prompt long-run after NDA. Procurement will join the final call — cc'd procurement@datapilot.ai.

If you can start the runs May 22 that works for us.

Best,
Sarah Lee
Head of ML Infrastructure, DataPilot
sarah.lee@datapilot.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 17:34:00 -0700
Subject: Perf results (summary) — A100 vs H100 vs L40S (full + MIG)

Ava / Team / Sarah (cc'd) —

Attached is the perf_matrix_20280528.csv with raw run-by-run metrics. High-level summary below (model: 13B-medium, 512 token streams unless noted). Runs executed in us-west-2, same container and runtime flags.

Summary (key metrics):
- H100 (full, 80GB)
  - TTFT median: 42 ms; p95: 118 ms; p99: 220 ms
  - Sustained throughput per GPU (512-token streams, 32 concurrent): ~18,500 tokens/sec
  - Max concurrent streams sustaining p95 < 180ms: 64 streams
  - Approx cost estimate: $1200 / 1M tokens (includes inferred GPU-hour amortized)

- A100 (full, 80GB)
  - TTFT median: 55 ms; p95: 165 ms; p99: 320 ms
  - Sustained throughput per GPU (512-token streams, 32 concurrent): ~14,000 tokens/sec
  - Max concurrent streams sustaining p95 < 180ms: 40 streams
  - Approx cost estimate: $980 / 1M tokens

- L40S (full, 48GB)
  - TTFT median: 68 ms; p95: 210 ms; p99: 430 ms
  - Sustained throughput per GPU (512-token streams, 32 concurrent): ~10,200 tokens/sec
  - Max concurrent streams sustaining p95 < 180ms: ~22 streams (p95 crosses 180ms at ~25)
  - Cost estimate: $650 / 1M tokens

MIG notes (1/2/4-way partitions):
- 1-way MIG (single partition ~full) tracked closely with full performance for the A100 but showed ~7-10% reduced throughput on H100 compared to full (likely kernel scheduling overhead).
- 4-way MIG (smaller partitions) provided better packing but increased TTFT by ~12-18% and reduced p95 headroom; good for high-concurrency, low-latency non-interactive batch workloads.

Sizing recommendations (based on pilot targets):
- Pilot profile: 100 QPS peak, average 75 tokens/request -> ~7.5k tokens/sec peak.
  - H100 full: 1 GPU sustains (~18.5k tokens/sec) — recommend 2 GPUs (1 active + 1 warm/failover) for pilot resilience.
  - A100 full: 1 GPU borderline (14k tokens/sec) — recommend 2 GPUs for pilot.
  - L40S: require 1-2 GPUs but p95 risks; recommend A100 or H100 for interactive flows.

Operational notes:
- For predictable latency at scale attach an autoscaler cap and prefer full GPUs for the interactive path. Use MIG for best-effort background batch scoring to increase utilization.
- We collected kernel/version flags in the CSV (columns: runtime_flags).

Next steps suggested:
1) Redwood to deliver a 1-page recommendation (we'll draft) and an estimate for a 3-month dedicated pilot pricing.
2) Procurement call to review cost model.

Attachments: perf_matrix_20280528.csv (detailed rows), run logs (linked in Drive).

-Karthik

Attachments: perf_matrix_20280528.csv (CSV 1.2MB)

Ava / Karthik —

Thanks for the clear summary and the CSV. We reviewed the numbers with product and procurement. Key takeaways:
- H100 looks like the only footprint that meets our p95 requirement consistently at target concurrency.
- We are sensitive to cost but willing to run H100 for the interactive path while using L40S/MIG for background batch scoring.

Procurement asks: please send the 3-month pilot quote and a simple SOW for the trial. We will sign NDA addendum and route the PO next week if the quote looks reasonable.

Can you also include the per-GPU hourly rate assumptions used in your $/1M token calc? That will help procurement map to our internal chargeback.

If you can email the quote and SOW by EOD Monday (June 5) we can try to align the procurement window.

Best,
Sarah Lee
Head of ML Infrastructure, DataPilot
